newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Singleton wants A$59 mln for TEN stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Singleton wants A$59 mln for TEN stake.

text.p: John Singleton Advertising Ltd (JSA) said on Friday it wanted to sell its five percent economic interest in television network The Ten Group Ltd for a total consideration of A$59.15 million.
The company said it was seeking to sell its 4.55 million shares for a gross price of A$13 cash per share, which values the network at A$1.18 billion.
JSA said its announcement was in accordance with the Ten shareholders agreement which included a pre-emptive rights deal with other shareholders.

The key shareholder in Ten is Canwest Global Communications Inc, which has a 57.5 percent economic interest but a voting interest of only 15 percent as it is a foreign-owned company and cannot raise its stake without government approval.

CanWest is controlled by Canadian media enterpreneur Izzy Asper who has said he wanted to retain his stake in Ten, if not increase it, and would support a share market float of the network if legal and tax problems could be resolved.
Telecasters North Queensland has a 20 percent voting stake and has said it would support a back-door listing of TEN through Telecasters, which has few operating assets.
Other individual shareholders in TEN are Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin, who along with Singleton each have voting stakes of 10 percent.
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said on Wednesday that these smaller shareholders want to sell their TEN shares but all investors are yet to agree on how the sale or float will occur.
